description: TELSS provides source code and documentation for calculating theoretical equilibrium lead(II) solubility. The US Environmental Protection Agency maintains the public repository and lists it among water modelling tools for infrastructure decisions. The repository identifies an R application and refers users to supplementary instructions accompanying the 2021 AWWA Water Science paper by Wahman and colleagues, Theoretical equilibrium lead(II) solubility revisited: Open source code and practical relationships. Users provide chemical conditions for an equilibrium calculation; this is not a geographic monitoring dataset or a time series of measured lead concentrations. Code is available free of charge under the MIT licence. The inspected README does not establish validated accuracy for a particular utility, pipe material or operating condition. An equilibrium prediction also does not, by itself, establish transient contaminant transport. The resource supports water-quality simulation for drinking-water infrastructure. EPANET is a related network model; no implemented coupling is claimed. Software, supplementary files and model outputs were not downloaded or executed.
